data.title: Atomic structures of the human immunophilin FKBP-12 complexes with FK506 and rapamycin
data.authors: Van Duyne GD; Standaert RF; Karplus PA; Schreiber SL; Clardy J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: X-ray structures of rapamycin sitting in FKBP12, the small protein it binds before it reaches mTOR. FKBP12 (a cone-shaped protein) holds rapamycin and the related drug FK506 in the same pocket, with a similar set of hydrogen bonds, and rapamycin keeps almost exactly the shape it has on its own. Because the two complexes block different steps of T-cell activation, the drugs' effects could not come from switching off FKBP12's own enzyme activity - the complex has to act on something else. For rapamycin that something turned out to be mTOR; the same lab showed the second half of the 'molecular glue' three years later (CHO1996).
data.abstract_excerpt: High resolution structures for the complexes formed by the immunosuppressive agents FK506 and rapamycin with the human immunophilin FKBP-12 have been determined by X-ray diffraction. FKBP-12 has a novel fold comprised of a five-stranded beta-sheet wrapping around a short alpha-helix with an overall conical shape. Both FK506 and rapamycin bind in the cavity defined by the beta-sheet, alpha-helix and three loops. Both FK506 and rapamycin bind in similar fashions with a set of hydrogen bonds and an unusual carbonyl binding pocket.

extracted_findings.effect: High-resolution structures of human FKBP12 bound to FK506 and to rapamycin; both drugs occupy the same binding pocket
